why: Three styles were made of the same cut; Document was chosen: « clearly the best ». Settled over twelve rounds, the result called « quasiment parfait » (2026-10-13).

name: Three ways: facecam, AI voice, hybrid
what: One skill, three modes: the whole video filmed with the real voice, no filming with an AI voice, or a filmed intro and cutbacks with the cloned voice for the rest.
when: Always: run.json › mode says which one; the app asks it first.
why: Ihsane: one skill, « YouTube video editor », for every horizontal video, filmed or not.

name: Intro cut right after the hook
what: The filmed intro stops at the end of the sentence that names the subject or the promise (within about 30 s); the plan of the video is the first thing the voice says after it.
when: Hybrid mode, and the first face shot of facecam.
why: Film only the intro, the clone does the rest: a faster process; the junction real voice → clone « ça passe ».

name: Filmed cutback
what: A short real line of the user (12 words at most, best a question) between two motion parts, cut 0.08 s before they speak and 0.13 s after their last word.
when: At most one per change of part; none when the take has none.
why: Past +0.13 s the next sentence's mouth movement shows.

name: Facecam: the real voice cut tight
what: The take's own voice runs all along: retakes, fillers and pauses over 0.5 s cut out, about 0.26 s of air between pieces, at the face shots' speed.
when: Facecam mode: face shots for the moments that need the face, motion parts for what is best shown.
why: « pas besoin de faire une voix avec Eleven Labs »; the same speed so the voice never changes pace between a face shot and a part.

when: Every filmed clip; the speed comes from profile.json › voiceover.introSpeed.
why: « je parle trop lentement… »: ×1.2 was tried and found too fast; ×1.1 kept.

name: Something changes every 1 to 2 s
what: An entry, a word rising, ink, a counter or the camera every 1 to 2 s; entries 0.3 to 0.6 s with a slight tilt and a bounce; every element has an entrance and an exit; soft shadows.
when: Always, in the motion parts.
why: A rule of the look (rule 13).
doc: references/look.md § The motion parts: the settled rules (rule 13)

name: No subtitles, no emoji, no title at the top left
what: The format carries no subtitles, no emoji and no title in the top left corner.
when: Never use them.
why: A rule of the look (rule 16); verify.mjs stops on subtitles.
doc: references/look.md § The motion parts: the settled rules (rule 16)

name: Never the spoken sentence on screen
what: The sentence the voice says is never written out on screen as a card of words; only short labels inside a schema.
when: Always, and above all in the motion scenes.
why: A schema makes the idea understood; written sentences only repeat the voice.
doc: references/motion-scenes.md § The techniques; plugins/video/skills/shorts/references/motion-pages.md § The bar

name: Cards appearing over and over
what: A long video made only of the engine's cards appearing one after the other.
when: Never for a whole long video: 2 or 3 key ideas become motion scenes, the rest stays in the blocks.
why: « la vidéo est un peu ennuyeuse… pas tout le temps faire des cartes comme ça qui apparaissent à l'écran de manière répétitive ».
doc: references/motion-scenes.md (intro); references/decisions.md § 2026-10-15 · v7 → v8 (extracts)

name: Motion scene (After Effects level)
what: One key idea told as a single After Effects-like scene over the whole 16:9 frame, written with gsap, rendered with alpha and laid as a screen of its own.
when: 2 or 3 per long video, 10–25 s each, on the ideas that carry the video; never the same scene twice for one concept; never on a screen recording or a face shot.
why: « j'aime bien les planches que t'as travaillées »: approved on the extracts.
doc: references/motion-scenes.md; references/decisions.md § 2026-10-15 · v7 → v8 (extracts)

name: The 3D floor
what: People as cards (drawn, never AI photos) standing on a floor in true perspective, the branches drawn on the floor; the camera pulls back, dives to one card with a reticle, then rides a yellow road along the branches; a card flips to a yellow back.
when: A hierarchy or a path between people (who decides, who influences).
why: One of the first three motion scenes, approved on the extracts.
doc: references/motion-scenes.md § The techniques

name: The type wall / type tree
what: Only type and ink: rank read in the font weight (thin → heavy on its word), a yellow highlighter swiping, a hand-drawn ink loop, short tags sticking on; the words regroup into a tree.
when: A selection out of a list, a classification, a definition.
why: One of the first three motion scenes, approved on the extracts.
doc: references/motion-scenes.md § The techniques

name: The elevator
what: A tower of floors with the frame as the shaft: big grey floor numerals in parallax, a rolling floor indicator, the camera following a yellow cable carrying a pill from floor to floor; the tower folds into one frame at the end.
when: A cascade, a sequence of levels or steps.
why: One of the first three motion scenes, approved on the extracts.
doc: references/motion-scenes.md § The techniques

name: Motion scene sounds: 3 at most, quiet
what: A motion scene has 3 sounds at most, quiet (−21 to −24 dB): whooshes on the camera's big moves, one soft landing, no click or pop per element.
when: Every motion scene (its cues are marked key so the sound pass keeps them).
why: Part of what all the approved scenes keep.
doc: references/motion-scenes.md § The techniques

name: Frame index with floor, never round
what: A frame index from a time is always floor(… + 1e-3), never round().
when: Every component that plays frames (motion scenes, screen shares).
why: The screen shares stuttered: round() on a 7.5-frame offset made ties, a frame repeated then one skipped.
doc: references/decisions.md § 2026-10-15 · v7 → v8 (extracts); references/engine.md § F.motionPage

name: Slides rebuilt, never shown
what: A screen recording of the user's slides is the reference for the diagrams, never on screen: every schema rebuilt in the look, node for node, explained on its words (the camera going in, pieces appearing, the rest pixelated or dimmed).
when: When the take has a screen share of slides.
why: « refaire les visuels avec un meilleur design, déplacer la caméra dessus, zoomer au bon endroit, entourer, highlighter ».
doc: SKILL.md § 7. The material; references/decisions.md § 2026-10-14 · a long facecam video

name: Drawings only on the whiteboard screens
what: Drawn schemas and notes go only on the drawn white screens: never on a face shot (no white notes behind the user), nothing over a screen share.
when: Always.
why: « tu me laisses tranquille ». No date is written for this rule in the docs.
doc: references/look.md § Long videos: chapters, the marker, the music

name: A shape casts its own shadow
what: A diamond, a node or a pill casts the shadow of its shape, never the square box of its element; soft blurred shadows only, never a hard offset shadow.
when: Always.
why: « tu gères mal les ombres » on the yellow diamonds.
doc: references/look.md § Long videos: chapters, the marker, the music; references/motion-scenes.md § The techniques

name: Stock shots in the frame on the paper
what: Real stock videos inside a thin ink frame on the paper (crosshairs, the fine screen-door grid, one grade for all, a slow push), 1.5 to 3 s each, on their words.
when: 8 to 12 per 4 minutes, where a picture says more than a card; never two full shots in a row; never where the film's graphics already say it.
why: Motion design alone « ça fait trop IA »; the version with stock and GIFs was « quasiment parfait ».
where: template/document/film/framed.js › F.framed; template/document/film/story.js › shot / shots; scripts/media.mjs
doc: references/media.md § In the film; references/decisions.md § 2026-10-13 · the media

name: GIFs as pinned prints
what: A known meme GIF in a pinned, torn, tilted print on the right with a short caption on a yellow label and « via GIPHY », the scene behind stepping back.
when: 3 to 5 per 4 minutes, 1.4 to 2.5 s each, on a sentence with a known meme; never full screen; organic use only.
why: A professional editor diversifies: « ça fait trop IA sinon ».
doc: references/media.md § In the film; references/decisions.md § 2026-10-13 · the media

name: Free commercial licences only
what: Stock shots only from Pexels or Mixkit's free licence; Mixkit « Restricted » clips refused; never a YouTube clip; GIFs organic use only.
when: Always.
why: Eight good Mixkit candidates carried the Restricted licence (personal use only).
doc: references/media.md § Licences: free commercial only

name: Full-screen 3D shots
what: Full-screen three.js shots between the moments (provider blocks stacking into a tower, line-art plans).
when: Not by default. Set aside for stock videos and GIFs.
why: Set aside: « stock videos + GIFs look better ». The motion scenes of 2026-10-15 are a different, approved thing.
doc: references/decisions.md § 2026-10-12/13 · the 3D shots, tried and SET ASIDE

name: Half-screen 3D, orbits of logos, stacked cylinders
what: 3D plans half-screen beside the 2D elements, a chip with an orbit of logos, stacked cylinders, a yellow ball travelling through blocks, a camera placed high or at random.
when: Never.
why: « un mauvais mélange »; the yellow ball « super moche »; the look « très Blender, basse qualité ».
doc: references/decisions.md § 2026-10-12/13 · the 3D shots, tried and SET ASIDE

name: Silences in float, never 8-bit
what: Every input of an audio concat is forced to float 48 kHz stereo, since ffmpeg's anullsrc silence is 8-bit and drags the voice to u8.
when: Every concat of a voice with a silence (chapter page pauses).
why: The sound « fait n'importe quoi » after the chapter pages: a loud broadband hiss on every word.
doc: SKILL.md § Traps already met; references/decisions.md § 2026-10-15 · v2 → v3

name: 1080p draft and 720p preview; 4K on request
what: A 1080p draft for review and a 720p preview to send in a chat; the 4K only when the user says so, drawn natively at 4K.
when: Every delivery.
why: « only once I tell you, we'll do the 4K render »; the big file would not open in a chat.
doc: SKILL.md § The rules that do not move (rule 12); references/decisions.md § 2026-10-13 · the render
